items.title: Greg Thomas interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: If I make certain judgments about you based on the pigment of your skin or your height or your weight or some attribute like that... It is absurd.

ctx.x: I wanted to talk about, I read this about you, under the banner of “Race and Jazz,” to shed light on the way that race has bedeviled the jazz discourse in the actual lives of jazz musicians. It’s a topic that gets written about a lot, and I’m wondering what you’re thinking about it at this point.

Well the intent of that series in All About Jazz was to, frankly to use the issue of race to point the way to culture. Because race biologically speaking is an illusion unless you’re talking about the human race. It almost sounds like a cliché but it’s true. But race certainly has — there’s a psychological and social and behavioral dimension to race that’s very real. Because if you believe, let’s take you Monk. If I make certain judgments about you based on the pigment of your skin or your height or your weight…
Okay, well and also you can make assumptions about, if we’re talking about musicians, where you’re going to be more likely to play in a certain way. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
